STEP 1 - Scene: A single whole apple (red-yellow variety) resting on a white square plate, photographed from directly above. Nothing else is on the plate.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is a square-ish white dish about 22 cm across its width. Vessel area is roughly 22 x 22 x 0.8 (rounded corners) ≈ 390 cm^2. The apple's diameter is about 1/3.5 of the plate width, so roughly 7 cm across. Treating the plate as a circle-equivalent of ~22 cm gives 3.14 x 11^2 ≈ 380 cm^2, consistent with the estimate.

STEP 3 - Items: One apple (whole, raw, unpeeled). No sauce, oil, or dressing visible.

STEP 4 - Area: Apple top view covers ~ π x 3.5^2 ≈ 38 cm^2, about 10% of the plate area.

STEP 5 - Volume: An apple is roughly a sphere-like solid of about 7 cm diameter, so volume ≈ (4/3)π(3.5)^3 ≈ 180 ml. Using the top-view envelope and a typical height gives a similar order, so take ~180 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Whole fruit is about 0.85 g/ml as a solid (it is dense, not a loose pile), giving ~150 g. Typical medium apple weighs 150–180 g, so ~160 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Raw apple ≈ 52 kcal/100 g. 160 g x 52/100 ≈ 83 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A single medium apple at ~160 g and ~80 kcal is plausible for what is visible. The plate contains nothing else, so no other items are added.

Total: ~160 g, ~83 kcal.
